system_description.narrative_title: Multipolar Stress: Wars, AI Boom and Monetary Tightening
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly coupled system driven by simultaneous security crises (Ukraine, the Middle East, regional conflicts in Africa and the Sahel), a resurgent and fractious technology boom centred on AI, and a common macroeconomic environment of higher rates and sticky inflation. Electoral volatility and shifting alliances amplify policy uncertainty while energy and supply‑chain shocks transmit local disruptions into global market and fiscal stress. Diplomatic activity and ad hoc ceasefires coexist with deep structural frictions — trade, cyber risk, and capital reallocation — producing high systemic sensitivity and the risk of cascading spillovers.
system_description.scope: Nation-states and coalitions, major and regional military conflicts, multilateral institutions, global capital and bond markets, central banks and monetary policy, multinational tech and energy firms, critical supply chains, cyber and information environments, and transnational non-state armed actors and humanitarian flows.
system_description.super_system: The globalized international political-economic-environmental system (the contemporary world order embedded in planetary economic and ecological constraints).
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial and monetary system (capital markets, central banks, sovereign debt)
Global technology and AI ecosystem (chip supply chains, cloud, enterprise AI demand)
Energy and commodity markets (oil, gas, LNG, strategic reserves)
Regional security architectures (Middle East diplomacy, Europe-Ukraine, Indo-Pacific)

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war
variables.description: The sustained military confrontation between Russia and Ukraine, with shifting frontlines, localized ceasefires and continued external military and diplomatic backing that are reshaping battlefield dynamics and peace prospects.

variables.name: Iran-led regional escalation
variables.description: A widening regional confrontation centered on Iran and Gulf actors, including proxy and maritime attacks on energy infrastructure and intense diplomacy aimed at preventing broader escalation.

variables.name: U.S.–China tech and trade rivalry
variables.description: Strategic competition between the United States and China over AI, semiconductors, data and trade policy that is driving export controls, investment shifts, sanctions and supply-chain realignment.

variables.name: Brazil political‑financial turmoil
variables.description: Domestic political upheaval and an unexpected electoral outcome in Brazil that are producing sharp market reactions and fiscal uncertainty, constraining policy space and posing regional contagion risks.

variables.name: Global monetary and market realignment
variables.description: Major central banks and global capital markets are reconfiguring as persistent inflation, rate‑cycle uncertainty and rising bond yields force policy pivots, alter asset allocations and amplify sovereign fiscal pressures.
